key_insight: HealthFound is a medical LLM designed to reason quantitatively over long-term patient data, turning longitudinal health records into actionable predictive reasoning.
clinical_relevance: It may help support earlier disease risk prediction and more robust interpretation of complex follow-up measurements in clinical and research settings.
method: Trained on 12.4 million examples, including 15-year longitudinal biomedical records from 501,936 participants.
Used a three-stage pipeline: progressive curriculum supervised fine-tuning, rejection-sampled retention fine-tuning, and task-verifiable policy optimization.
Combined cohort data with medical knowledge and general reasoning tasks to improve quantitative reasoning.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on 1,162 UK Biobank prediction tasks, eight public medical benchmarks, and external validations in MIMIC-IV and NHANES, with reported gains of 6%+ across 484 disease endpoints.
watch_item: Because the model is trained and tested on complex retrospective datasets, real-world deployment would still need careful validation for bias, calibration, and workflow fit.
paper_title: HealthFound: a health world model for quantitative reasoning on longitudinal health profiles
